title: Platform activation ops roadmap & tenant cutover huddle
next_steps: Redwood: send tenant cutover runbook draft and staging checklist
MarlinGrid: provide staging VPC peering details and SSO test user
Schedule dry-run cutover window (2 hours) week of Aug 9
SE to run baseline latency/throughput test against sample dataset
action_items: Evan Cho - share staging runbook and smoke-test scripts by 2026-08-03
Tom Bell - provision staging VPC peering and share CIDR by 2026-08-02
Priyanka Rao - confirm KMS key policy and compliance questionnaire answers by 2026-08-05
Jordan Meyers - send pricing addendum and suggested canary plan by 2026-07-31
summary: Kickoff huddle to align on runbook, tenant cutover windows, security checkpoints, and smoke-test scope for MarlinGrid's platform activation. Focus on staging network, SSO/KMS readiness, rollback plan, and performance benchmarks. Agreed dry-run and clear owners for next two weeks.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Meyers: ok thanks everyone for joining, uh today's a short ops huddle to align on the tenant cutover and runbook for MarlinGrid's activation. i'll run through the agenda quick, then evan will go over smoke tests and lena will cover success criteria.
[01:08] Rashida Khan: sounds good, appreciate it. we've got some pressure from product to have the chat features into staging by mid-August, so timeline is tight.
[02:16] Lena Ortiz: noted, mid-August aligns with our proposed dry-run week of Aug 9. main things we need: staging VPC peering, an SSO test user, and confirmation on KMS.
[03:22] Tom Bell: on the VPC peering, i can provision but need to know the Redwood side CIDR and whether you want route or proxy mode.
[04:10] Evan Cho: we usually recommend route-based peering for lower lat, but proxy is fine if your network team prefers it. also note the Dedicated pool will show up as "Redwood Dedicate" in some logs — auto transcript fun.
[05:05] Priyanka Rao: on KMS, we need to ensure customer-managed keys and audit logs go to our SIEM. does Redwood support AWS KMS and HSM?
[05:48] Evan Cho: yes, you can bring your own KMS keys via ARN, and we support HSM workflows through the private deploy package. there are a couple of service account perms we'll list in the runbook.
[06:30] Marcus Li: quick question on data residency — our legal team requires tokens not be stored beyond 30 days, and we need S3 access logs retained 12 months. is that doable?
[07:12] Lena Ortiz: yep we can set retention windows; for hosted we'll need to confirm the plan tier, but for Private/Dedicated we can enforce retention and log forwarding.
[08:00] Jordan Meyers: let's lock in who signs the runbook once it's final. rashida, is it you or tom?
[08:22] Rashida Khan: i'll own approval with priya as compliance sign-off.
[09:01] Jordan Meyers: perfect. Evan, can you walk through the smoke-tests and metrics you plan to run?
[09:45] Evan Cho: sure. short list: 1) basic generation latency at varying sequence lengths, 2) KV cache warm vs cold, 3) burst throughput with our batcher, 4) memory/oom monitoring. scripts will be in a repo. note: sometimes the transcript reads 'KV cash' but it's "KV cache".
[11:02] Tom Bell: for burst tests, we need to know the recommended batch size — we currently run with our internal in-house endpoints at batch size 8.
[11:46] Evan Cho: baseline we'll try batch sizes 1, 4, 8 and 16, and also test quantized model variants if you want to see TCO impact. Marcus: is model fidelity a hard requirement for go-live?
[12:30] Marcus Li: fidelity must be within our current thresholds — no drop in accuracy over our eval set more than 1.5%. we can share the eval set.
[13:10] Priyanka Rao: i want to confirm audit logs: will every API call be logged with token-level metadata available? we need to map to our proto schema.
[13:48] Lena Ortiz: yes, we export request-level metadata and cost/latency breakdowns; we'll send the mapping doc.
[14:26] Rashida Khan: about cutover window — product ideally wants zero downtime, but we know model switch overs can be tricky. what's Redwood's canary/fallback approach?
[15:05] Evan Cho: recommendation is 3-step: smoke small percentage traffic to the new tenant (1-5%), monitor latency/errors for 15 minutes, ramp to 25% then to 100%. fallback is instant to prior model/endpoint; we keep a pinned variant for rollback.
[16:20] Tom Bell: what about tokenization differences causing output drift — any tools to compare?
[16:58] Evan Cho: we'll provide side-by-side generation diffs and an automated regression harness for your eval set; takes about an hour to run at staging scale.
[18:05] Marcus Li: timeline check — if we do dry-run week of Aug 9, when would production cutover be?
[18:46] Jordan Meyers: earliest safe is Aug 16 assuming dry-run goes well; we can shift. we'll make a contingency plan for the week after.
[19:30] Priyanka Rao: legal wants SOC2 and ISO references plus evidence of pen-test. do you have a current report?
[19:58] Lena Ortiz: yes, we'll attach our SOC2 Type II summary and an ISO outline; for pen-test we can provide scope and recent remediation notes.
[20:40] Rashida Khan: also can you provide a sample runbook excerpt showing rollback steps? especially around stateful caches and prefix keys.
[21:12] Evan Cho: yes, runbook will include cache invalidation steps, KV cache flush commands, and how to revert prefix caches; we sometimes see transcriptions that call it 'KV cash' but it's 'KV cache flush'.
[22:00] Tom Bell: access model: we want RBAC roles mapped to our AD groups. is SAML attribute mapping supported?
[22:37] Lena Ortiz: yes SAML/SCIM support, and we can map attributes to roles. send the group names and we'll propose mappings.
[23:15] Jordan Meyers: good. on observability, what alerts should we set before cutting over?
[23:50] Evan Cho: errors per second spike, 95th/99th latency breaches, token-per-request cost anomaly, and drop in successful generation ratio. we'll share recommended alert thresholds.
[24:38] Marcus Li: for the canary, do you need our prod traffic routing changes, or can you handle traffic splits from your side?
[25:18] Evan Cho: we can do traffic splits at the platform layer for hosted/dedicated traffic; for private you'll need a routing rule but we can provide the config snippet.
[26:05] Rashida Khan: about test data — we will provide a representative dataset but sanitized. any constraints on size?
[26:36] Evan Cho: couple hundred prompts is fine for functional smoke; for perf tests we'll use a larger synthetic load generator that replicates your distribution.
[27:20] Tom Bell: security checklist aside, we also need to run a penetration checklist — who does that? internal or can Redwood assist?
[27:55] Priyanka Rao: ideally Redwood shares scope; our security team will run the checks but would like coordination.
[28:30] Lena Ortiz: we'll assign a security liaison and include Redwood's security contact in the thread.
[29:05] Jordan Meyers: circling back to responsibilities: rashida approves, priya signs compliance, tom executes peering, evan provides scripts, lena tracks the playbook.
[29:45] Rashida Khan: yep, put that in the runbook.
[30:12] Jordan Meyers: ok we'll create a timeline and a 2-week checklist. who's comfortable with a 2-hour dry-run window?
[30:50] Marcus Li: 2 hours is acceptable. we may need a longer fallback window if we encounter issues.
[31:25] Evan Cho: during dry-run we'll do a staged set: step 1 baseline smoke, step 2 1-5% canary for 15 min, step 3 ramp to 25% for 30 min, step 4 full switch. each step has go/no-go gates in the runbook.
[32:10] Tom Bell: do we need changes to our firewall for peering? i can loop in networking.
[32:36] Jordan Meyers: provide the CIDR we'll need, tom, and we'll confirm ports — mostly 443 but we'll include endpoints.
[33:05] Priyanka Rao: question: will request bodies leave our VPC in any way? we need an assurance that payloads are not persisted beyond retention windows.
[33:40] Lena Ortiz: for Private/Dedicated, payloads are kept per customer retention; we can guarantee deletion per agreed retention policy and provide logs for audit.
[34:15] Rashida Khan: also curious about cost tracking — we need token-level cost reporting broken down by route/model.
[34:52] Lena Ortiz: Redwood Console has token-level breakdowns per model and per route, and we'll enable a dashboard for you.
[35:30] Marcus Li: any recommended throttles to avoid sudden cost spikes during cutover?
[35:58] Evan Cho: yes, we recommend a token cap per minute and per-user rate limit during ramp. we'll include default values and you can tune.
[36:40] Tom Bell: in the staging peering, what's the expected latency to your dedicated pool?
[37:05] Evan Cho: typical p95 is sub-80ms for nearby regions; we'll run bench tests and share numbers for your exact region. last time the transcript auto-changed 'p95' to 'pis nine' which was fun.
[37:50] Jordan Meyers: we should schedule the bench test — evan, you and tom coordinate on dataset and keys.
[38:20] Evan Cho: will do. i'll push scripts to the repo and share the link.
[38:55] Rashida Khan: for SSO test user, we'll create a service account named mg-test-sso and share credentials via secure vault.
[39:25] Priyanka Rao: and for KMS we'll give you an ARN with limited access.
[39:50] Jordan Meyers: great. any blockers from MarlinGrid side we should know now?
[40:12] Tom Bell: just bandwidth on networking; otherwise mostly policy questions.
[40:38] Marcus Li: product wants to see end-to-end demo during dry-run — is that possible?
[41:02] Evan Cho: absolutely, we'll include an end-to-end scenario in the smoke tests.
[41:40] Jordan Meyers: ok let's call out deliverables and dates — evan to share scripts by Aug 3, tom to share VPC details by Aug 2, priya to finalize KMS by Aug 5, jordan to send pricing/canary plan by tomorrow.
[42:25] Rashida Khan: noted. please also include a list of logs and where they'll be exported.
[42:48] Lena Ortiz: we'll include cloudwatch and S3 export mapping in the runbook.
[43:22] Marcus Li: one more: are there any model conversion or quantization steps that could alter outputs noticeably? we need to be aware if you recommend quantized variants to reduce cost.
[43:58] Evan Cho: quantization can slightly alter outputs; we'll run the eval harness and show delta metrics; if unacceptable, we stick to full fidelity.
[44:40] Tom Bell: for rollback, how long does cache warmup take after we revert?
[45:05] Evan Cho: depends on workload; typically 10-20 minutes for KV cache to warm for common prefixes, longer for cold starts. runbook includes a warming plan.
[45:46] Jordan Meyers: good — i'll make sure those times are explicit. any final security items?
[46:10] Priyanka Rao: just that our compliance team wants an SSO audit trail and access revocation steps documented.
[46:42] Lena Ortiz: we'll add a step-by-step SSO revoke procedure.
[47:05] Rashida Khan: can we get a table of escalation contacts for the dry-run? who at Redwood do we call for an immediate rollback?
[47:28] Jordan Meyers: contact list will include evan as primary, lena as secondary, and a 24/7 on-call number if you have an enterprise SLA. i'll include names and pager rotations.
[48:05] Marcus Li: perfect. i think we have alignment.
[48:30] Evan Cho: quick note, sometimes the transcript mislabels my voice as 'Speaker 3' but that's fine.
[49:00] Jordan Meyers: ok let's recap: runbook draft and scripts by Aug 3, peering details by Aug 2, compliance sign-off by Aug 5, dry-run week of Aug 9 (2-hour window) and potential prod cutover Aug 16. owners captured in action items.
[50:12] Rashida Khan: thanks all. any blockers?
[50:35] Tom Bell: none from me.
[50:50] Priyanka Rao: none.
[51:05] Jordan Meyers: i'll send meeting notes and the initial runbook draft within 24 hours. thanks everyone, talk soon.
[51:30] [meeting ends]
